directives.name: The Victorious Federation
directives.title: The Victorious Federation
directives.desc:
At last, Central Siberia has been united under our authority, with our rivals in the region vanquished and their loyalists scattered, forced into hiding or exile. However, for the continued success of our Federation, much work remains to be done.

First there is the matter of consolidating our gains, by integrating the new territories more closely and securing our boundaries. Then we must consider how to stabilize our rule and satisfying the people, in hopes of restoring the law, order, and stability that is so desperately needed. Many problems remain, but beyond them lies a bright future for the Federation.

directives.name: The Siberian Economy
directives.title: The Siberian Economy
directives.desc:
Our consolidation of Central Siberia has opened up to us the vast wealth and potential that lies within Siberia. Siberia contains the potential to become the foundation of a strong Russian state, one that will extend its might from the Pacific to Moscow.

In order to properly realise Siberia's potential we must leverage our already impressive industrial base to exploit the wealth of the region. With the help of the National Champions, our economic growth will be truly frightening to behold.

directives.name: Expand the All-Siberian Army
directives.title: Expand the All-Siberian Army
directives.desc:
Although we have recently made great gains in our efforts towards the reunification of Russia, we still control only a fraction and much work remains to be done to ensure the continued success of our armed forces.

The first step in this is to expand the army, making it larger, stronger, and deadlier than ever before, to the point where our enemies will crumble before it. Many other areas of the military need to be developed, but this is the simplest and easiest one. The soldiers of the Federation march ever onwards.

directives.name: Our Geopolitical Future
directives.title: Our Geopolitical Future
directives.desc:
With the Federation's position secure, and Russia quickly stabilizing under our rule, we can begin looking outwards towards the world. Given the relatively non-ideological nature of our government, we find ourselves with great diplomatic opportunities.

Japan and its Sphere seem happy to deal with us and our corporations, as does the United States, which has even indicated it would support us in a conflict between us and Germany. The Federation's future is still uncertain, but if we can secure allies to help defend us, and trade agreements to reinforce our economy, there will be nothing we can't do.

directives.name: Bread and Games
directives.title: Bread and Games
directives.desc:
Above all else, everyday people desire just two things: bread to feed themselves with, and games with which to entertain them. So long as these are provided and made easily accessible, there will be little cause for unhappiness and unrest among the people, and therefore very little room for extremist organizations to grow and gain strength.

While some sacrifices must be made to achieve this, they are more than worth the current and future stability of our state.

directives.name: Appoint New Governors
directives.title: Appoint New Governors
directives.desc:
Although the practice of appointing military governors of freshly conquered territories has served us very well, it was always intended to be a temporary measure due to the fragile nature of the situation we were in.

Now that we are in a more secure position, it is finally time to make good on our promise to remove them, and appoint new ones in their place to aid the integration into the Federation of new lands, as well as the restoration of stability and reduction of popular unrest.

directives.name: Establish Educational Standards
directives.title: Establish Educational Standards
directives.desc:
How can we hope to cultivate a world-class economy when our people continue to go about their lives without an education to speak of? To say that our education system is in shambles would allude to the existence of such a system to begin with. In reality, any semblance of a proper schooling body fell into the abyss along with the rest of the Soviet Union over two decades ago.

Let us finally lay out the groundwork for a proper education system. We shall develop new curricula and guidelines for the classrooms, to make sure that the students of the Federation are being taught in the ways of the modern world.

directives.name: Repurpose the Siberian Plan
directives.title: Repurpose the Siberian Plan
directives.desc:
Up until now, the Federation's industrial might has been built on the back of Bukharin's Siberian Plan. While the Siberian Plan was by far Bukharin's greatest achievement, it cannot be denied that the industrial base it was responsible for has been lagging behind in the march of progress.

We should use the plan as a template with which to create a modern and improved plan in order to meet the needs of a modern industrial state. It will be up to the industrial theorists and brilliant minds of the Federation to build this new plan, but when it is complete our industrial might will be unassailable within Russia.

directives.name: Supervise the Agricultural Sector
directives.title: Supervise the Agricultural Sector
directives.desc:
The lands of the Altay near Novosibirsk are incredibly fertile, being almost without compare in the region and a potentially invaluable asset to our plans.

However, attempts to make use of this natural bounty are impeded by the great disarray and inefficiency present in our agricultural sector, a problem that we are increasingly forced to give our attention to prevent it from worsening.

Fortunately for us, there is a simple solution to this, which is establishing firm and vigilant supervision of the whole sector, allowing us to streamline and organize it.

directives.name: The Siberian Air Fleet
directives.title: The Siberian Air Fleet
directives.desc:
The air forces of the Federation have always been one of its greatest advantages, soaring above to rain fiery death upon those of our enemies unlucky enough to be below them, and shooting down any foolish enough to try and oppose them in the air.

However, it is becoming clear that it is growing severely outdated, the planes little more than toys in comparison to those fielded by many modern states. We must begin work immediately to modernize and improve our air fleet, and close the technological gap of our proudest military branch.

directives.name: Incorporate New Territorial Armies
directives.title: Incorporate New Territorial Armies
directives.desc:
Many of the lands conquered by the Federation fielded impressive armies when they still had their independence, even if they weren't so impressive as to be able to prevent defeat and annexation by us.

It would be wise to incorporate the best of these forces into our own military, growing it significantly and allowing us to have them fight those we face next. Though we must be cautious, so that our armed forces do not become infested with extremists, we also cannot afford to be too picky in these chaotic times.

directives.name: Travel to the East
directives.title: Travel to the East
directives.desc:
Our position in Central Siberia is secure, and the time has come to turn our attention back to the world. To revive our dormant foreign service and once more make our presence known, however, reduced we may be.

So, we turn east to the lands of the Empire of the Rising Sun, across the Mongolian Steppe, and to the Land of the Free, our neighbors across the Arctic Circle. Russia is back!

directives.name: Missions to Our Neighbors
directives.title: Missions to Our Neighbors
directives.desc:
Though we might seek allies abroad, it would be unwise to neglect those states neighboring us, allowing our relationships with them to deteriorate. These include the Kazakhs, their future long since tied to that of Russia, the Chinese, once our rivals in the east and now a promising opportunity, and the Mongols, caught between us and the Sphere.

Until Russia is reunited, conflict with outside states is one of the last things we can afford. Additionally, much of our economy depends on trade with our neighbors, and we must avoid lost profit where we can.

directives.title: Enshrine the Silovik State
directives.desc:
We must push forward with the idea of a state built on the principles of national stabilization and strength above all else, and managed by military officers who have proven their competence.

Effective and capable men are necessary to unite all of Russia under the Federation, and the past failure of states such as the Central Siberian Republic, which thought of stability and security as secondary concerns, has only proven further the necessity of this structure for the sake of peace.

directives.name: The Vestiges of Revolt
directives.title: The Vestiges of Revolt
directives.desc:
The scars of the Workers' Revolt still remain, and if nothing is done soon they will continue to fester unabated. We must remind the working class of Siberia that no matter what their grievances may be with our administration, rebellion will not be tolerated.

In addition to repairing the damage still left over from the fighting, we will restore order to the industrial sectors of the region and let any potential dissenters know that we are still in charge. Several methods have been proposed, and it will ultimately be up to our wise and noble President to decide which would be the best course of action.

directives.title: Grants for Research and Development
directives.desc:
We're never going to be able to stay ahead of our rivals when the entire Federation still uses technological methods that wouldn't look out of date thirty years ago. Unfortunately, having an advanced society is a bit more complicated than just waiting for skilled scientists and technicians to appear.

To speed the process along, we shall strategically designate certain sectors within the nation to receive specialized grants to aid research and development. Once we grease the wheels a little, the next generation of scientists will be within our reach.

directives.title: Promote the National Champions

directives.name: Expand the Factory City
directives.title: Expand the Factory City
directives.desc:
Novosibirsk is widely known as a "factory city"; an industrial lynchpin that is sometimes regarded as more of a giant factory than a place where people make their homes. Indeed, this city is the most industrialized in all of Siberia, and we see no reason why we shouldn't embrace this fact.

With the help of our loyal "national champions", Novosibirsk shall be expanded far beyond its current, already extensive capabilities. This city shall be one that never rests; where the factories stretch beyond that which the eye can see, and work day and night to build a stronger, safer future for all of us.

directives.name: Subsidies for Mechanization
directives.title: Subsidies for Mechanization
directives.desc:
The Siberian peasantry has so long been utilizing awfully outdated methods and techniques, with some of them dating from the times of the Tsars. This backwardness produces two worrying consequences for our Federation: A low agricultural output and large swaths of our workforce being tied up in inefficient activities.

We will mechanize our countryside. With subsidies and loans, our farms will be able to afford the most modern machinery, rapidly increasing production and breaking our reliance on large numbers of manual laborers.

directives.name: Inspect Japanese Jets
directives.title: Inspect Japanese Jets
directives.desc:
The Empire of Japan shares plenty of the blame with the Nazis for the fall of the old Union and the fracturing of Russia. They occupy rightful Russian lands and are unmatched in their arrogance, and yet it cannot be denied that they are a world leader in technology.

The Japanese are especially adept in the area of aviation. Though it would be easy to turn our noses up at the Japanese and their technology, for now we must swallow our pride and study the designs of their jet aircraft.

For the good of the Federation.

directives.name: Siberian War Doctrines
directives.title: Siberian War Doctrines
directives.desc:
Fighting across nearly the entire breadth of Siberia taught us much in the ways of fighting Siberian warfare. We came up against many forces, unique in their doctrines and methods of warfare, and though we did eventually come out victorious, there were certainly instances in which forces even smaller than our own managed to inflict heavy losses on us, and even eke out a few small tactical victories.

We should seek to incorporate these practices and doctrines that our fallen foes utilized, so that we might further professionalize our fighting force. We can only become stronger for it.

directives.name: Lessons of the Unification Wars
directives.title: Lessons of the Unification Wars
directives.desc:
War is a punishing teacher, and every mistake made is an advantage given to the enemy. Throughout the Siberian Unification Wars we learned a great deal about our armed forces' effectiveness, its strengths, its skills, and most importantly, its weaknesses.

These past few wars have exposed some glaring weaknesses in our army. They taught us what our soldiers were good at, and what they were very poor at. These were hard-won lessons, and must not be forgotten as we work to improve and modernize our military doctrine. Let's ensure that our military isn't forced to learn these lessons again.

directives.name: Establish Japanese Relations
directives.title: Establish Japanese Relations
directives.desc:
Russia has, at this point, had a decently long history with Japan, and much of it isn't good. Despite that, Japan remains one of the globe's foremost superpowers, and its influence, much like Germany's or the United States', stretches far across the globe.

It would be foolish of us not open diplomatic ties with the Sphere and start working on improving our relations. Besides, history needn't dictate the future. It so happens that our governments and economic setups are rather alike, and cooperation between our two nations could bring about great prosperity. Let us see what we make happen.

directives.name: The Twin Eagles
directives.title: The Twin Eagles
directives.desc:
Across the Pacific, America enticingly beckons to us. Among the three great superpowers currently manipulating politics globally, the United States has shown itself to be the most stable of the three. Like ourselves, they recognize the benefits that business can bring, and utilize such industrial strengths to become one of the most powerful nations on Earth even before the Second World War.

Though there are those who wouldn't consider us as democratic as, say, the old Central Siberian Republic once was, the United States has demonstrated a willingness in the past to support such governments regardless provided they are working against Germany or Japan. We should exploit this by reaching out, and seeing what deals can be made.

directives.name: Partnerships in China
directives.title: Partnerships in China
directives.desc:
In spite of domination and exploitation by the Japanese, China has become a truly large market, with easy and largely secure investments, and it only continues to grow as time passes.

Though their ability to act on their own is limited, we will reach out to them within the boundaries they possess under the watchful eye of the Sphere, and forge economic and strategic partnerships to whatever extent we can to strengthen both parties and allow us greater access to and influence in the markets of East Asia.

directives.name: A Kazakh Consulate
directives.title: A Kazakh Consulate
directives.desc:
For centuries, the futures of Kazakhstan and Russia have been inextricably linked, and the present is no different. Much like us, the Kazakhs have suffered tremendously from war, banditry, and abject poverty.

However, they have overcome these difficulties just as we did, and are beginning to recover their past greatness. We should immediately dispatch an emissary to reach out to them, in order to establish formal relations and celebrate the beginning of the end of our shared tribulations.

directives.name: Connections with Mongolia
directives.title: Connections with Mongolia
directives.desc:
Caught between two worlds, one that of a rising sun beginning to set, and the other a Russian bear coming out of hibernation to avenge its humiliation, the Mongols must align with one or the other to protect themselves in an increasingly restless Asia.

Obviously, it would be in our best interest to make every effort to convince them of the benefits of aligning with us. We will initiate talks to improve our relationship with them, securing our trade in the region and ensuring a stable buffer state against the Sphere for the time being.

directives.name: Reward Our Allies
directives.title: Reward Our Allies
directives.desc:
Promises are promises, and we made quite a few of them to our corporate friends during our time of crisis. Now that we are in less immediate danger, they expect these promises to be kept, and our government has always at least met expectations.

We shall grant them new and more generous contracts with the Federation, to allow them to expand into and exploit the resources of the new territories under our control. This will make their past investments into our cause profitable and convince them that continued cooperation with us would be in their best interest.

directives.name: Trust in the Party of Power
directives.title: Trust in the Party of Power
directives.name_en: Trust in the Party of Power
directives.title_en: Trust in the Party of Power
directives.desc:
What is needed above all else by the people is prosperity for them and stability of the state, and we cannot rely on popular will to bring this about. Democracy has failed us in the past, and giving it another chance would be a serious, and possibly fatal, mistake.

Instead, our objective should be solidifying our control over the state apparatus and levers of power, in order to centralize the powers of the government and give the people what they should have, even if it is not what they want.

directives.name: A Nod to Democracy
directives.title: A Nod to Democracy
directives.desc:
Though it might seem unwise to rely once more on a system that failed us all miserably, there is an argument to be made for allowing the masses a greater measure of democracy, mainly that it would serve to placate those hesitant to accept our government.

This would take the form of minor concessions and reforms within the state, as well as opening more leadership positions to civilians and supporters of democratic power. Of course, we would not go so far as to allow the people to have real power over us, but by appearing to scale back our control over them, they might be more eager to serve our purposes.

directives.name: The Sovereign Security Act
directives.title: The Sovereign Security Act
directives.desc:
No preventative measures are too drastic when the safety of our people is on the line! Terrorists and would-be revolutionaries lurk behind every corner, and our current means of dealing with them simply is not sufficient any longer. A stronger, more iron-fisted approach is necessary.

The Sovereign Security Act will be our savior in these dark times. Our counter-insurgency forces will enjoy increased funding and supplies to perform their duties with enhanced efficiency, while certain political liberties abused by our hidden foes will be cracked down on. This is not likely to be a popular act with our people, but hopefully they will realize the necessity of such measures when our streets are safe again.

directives.title: Sensible Concessions
directives.desc:
Some would suggest that an iron-clad hand is necessary to prevent unrest amongst the labor, but they fail to realize that such methods would only inflame working man's anger even more. The last thing we need right now is to pour gasoline on the embers of the last disaster, so perhaps a different approach is needed.

We shall reach out to prominent union leaders and labor activists to work out some sort of arrangement that would be best for both parties. If successful, we will kill two birds with one stone: our workers will have no reason to revolt against us, and our industry can finally achieve its past glories. All that remains now is to make the arrangements.

directives.name: Consolidate the Energy Sector
directives.title: Consolidate the Energy Sector
directives.desc:
Under the soil of Siberia lie vast reserves of oil and natural gas, fuel hydrocarbons, the lifeblood of the modern age. Until now, those riches lay mostly unexplored, but that must end very soon. We must organize and consolidate the energy extraction industry.

No longer to be left in the hands of small companies and adventurers, the nature of this business demands intense capital, and our government will grant that. With the guarantee of profit to our private partners and investors by way of an established monopoly and government inputs, the Siberian energy sector will be genuinely efficient.

directives.name: A Mind to Living Standards
directives.title: A Mind to Living Standards
directives.desc:
Economies exist to support states, and states, in turn, exist to support the lives of the people that live under them. Our economy, our state, neither are exempt from these rules. As we continue our efforts to reunite Russia, and our economy expands with our borders, so too will our state have to make use of this expanded economy to improve the lives of its citizens.

If we do not, we run the risk of inspiring a level of popular unrest we can't afford to have at such a critical moment. As such, we will devote more of our industrial output to the creation of various products that make the lives of consumers easier and more convenient.

directives.desc:

The factories of Novosibirsk will start assembling Kamov's model of a coaxial rotor utility helicopter, unlike anything our enemies have. This fast mobile transport will give our troops a cutting edge on the battlefield.

directives.name: Revise the Training Programs
directives.title: Revise the Training Programs
directives.desc:
Having incorporated many army's doctrines and many armies themselves into our military, we have discovered many inadequacies in our training regimens and army induction process as a whole.

It would do us well to rework our training corps so that we might start putting out more professionalized soldiers as we move away from the mercenary type training we used before, utilizing the doctrines and procedures we have adopted from these other subjugated warlords. Hopefully, this will allow us to improve our army's long term effectiveness.

directives.name: Propose the Mongolian Pipeline
directives.title: Propose the Mongolian Pipeline
directives.desc:
One of Japan's greatest weaknesses has always been natural resources. The ravenous Japanese economy simply never had enough on the home isles to sustain itself. It's a big part of why Japan went on to conquer so much of Asia. Their war machine simply could not function without the coal of Manchuria and oil of Indonesia.

Even now, an inefficient Sphere still struggles to keep up with the material demands of Japan. Fortunately for us, resources have always been among Russia's greatest strengths. We produce almost everything, and in great amounts as well. We should see if Japan wouldn't be opposed to the construction of a pipeline through Mongolia to facilitate materials trade between our two nations.

directives.name: Discuss Arctic Partnerships
directives.title: Discuss Arctic Partnerships
directives.desc:
Though relatively underutilized from a trade perspective, the Arctic region offers unique benefits for those around it - including ourselves.

For Russia, not only is it a viable trade route through which we can ship goods to the Atlantic now that we've lost the former Leningrad, but it is also an avenue through which we can exert our own political power and potentially align some nations with our own.

We should reach out to other Arctic countries, and see what economic partnerships can be made between our industrialists and theirs.

directives.name: A Controlled Political Spectrum
directives.title: A Controlled Political Spectrum
directives.desc:
Although they have little actual chance of taking power again, it's always wisest not to underestimate the ambitions of the extreme movements of the left and right.

In order to weaken them, and therefore strengthen our government, we will play them against each other, distracting them with their petty ideological struggle while convincing the people of their dangerous and violent nature, thereby slowly reducing them to irrelevancy without us having to act openly against them. By doing so, we will take control of all politics in the Federation, and keep the demagogues in check.

directives.name: Maintaining the Equilibrium
directives.title: Maintaining the Equilibrium
directives.desc:
For the first time in many months, our cities are finally returning to their pre-revolt orderliness, but there is still work to be done. Old ghosts from the unification wars still haunt our new territories to this very day, and they will need to be excorcized if our Federation wishes to move forward into a bold new future.

A heightened police presence will dissuade our new subjects from any foolish action, but a strong show of force is only half the battle. Meetings will be held with the provincial governors and mayors across Siberia to discuss the best way to finish the integration of these troubled lands. With luck, we won't have to give too many concessions in the name of stability.

With the aid of our good friends and allies in the National Champions it is only a matter of time before the vast wealth of Siberia will be available to us in quantities unheard of before.

The riches of Siberia must be exploited for the good of the Federation.

directives.name: A Central Design Bureau
directives.title: A Central Design Bureau
directives.desc:
Research of new and improved technologies and designs to implement them for practical use are critical to the advancement of our state, but both have a certain risk to them. Left uncontrolled and undirected, research and design can easily become useless, or even counterproductive.

To protect against this and ensure efficient and coordinated scientific work, we will establish a Central Design Bureau, responsible for oversight of all practical research, the design of new technologies, and the organization of all scientific efforts.

directives.title: A Bipolar Partnership
directives.desc:
At last, we have taken the necessary steps towards decisively aligning ourselves with a powerful Pacific government and deepening the association between us, finally creating a partnership with them certain to stand the test of time.

While this decision came with no shortage of controversy from those who had favored a deal with the other power, it is done and there is nothing they can do about it now. There is little reason for them to be bitter, either; we have reaped great rewards from our improved trade with our chosen partners, and the benefits have been seen by everyone that matters.

directives.name: Consider Barnaul's Position
directives.title: Consider Barnaul's Position
directives.desc:
Novosibirsk may be the administrative center of the Federation, but the adjacent city of Barnaul is also an important lynchpin in our nation. Its mayor, Vasily Shukshin, has quickly grown to be the second most powerful politician within the halls of power, and his particular views on how the state should be run have become more prominent as well.

Unfortunately, Shukshin's rise has caused some rather predictable tension with his main rival: President Pokryshkin. In order to put a stop to this bickering before it gets out of control, perhaps it would be prudent to reach out to Shukshin and see if he's willing to compromise in some way.

After all, if a ship changes its course only slightly, the destination shall be entirely different. In this instance, our destination is a strong and stable Russia.

After all, an ignorant citizen is a content citizen...

directives.name: Special Administrative Zones
directives.title: Special Administrative Zones
directives.desc:
Our foes during the unification wars were a diverse bunch, if nothing else. From the mad monarchists of Kemerovo to the armchair philosophers and artists of Tomsk; they all had vastly different approaches to governing their lands, and bafflingly enough? Most of them worked.

Why change what is already working? As long as these regions remain loyal to us, there is no need to crack down on them. "Special Administrative Zones" have been established in these formerly hostile territories to continue the administrative methods of their previous owners, while still bringing them in line with our own ideals of governance. Any regions whose administration cannot be adapted, however, can always be granted to our friends in the industrial sector...

directives.name: Infantry Support Vehicle Designs
directives.title: Infantry Support Vehicle Designs
directives.desc:
Modern warfare requires vehicles that are both capable and reliable. Operating across the vast distances and in the harsh climate of Siberia, we have become well accustomed in what makes an effective vehicle.

Despite that, we remain dependent on foreign or pre-war vehicles for almost all of our needs. Not only are these foreign goods of dubious quality when they arrive here, they are often not suited for the demands we place on them. We will, therefore, design new, domestic vehicles specifically for our needs in this demanding environment, and in so doing ensure our army's effectiveness and viability.

directives.name: A Siberian MBT
directives.title: A Siberian MBT
directives.desc:
In a similar vein to our motorized vehicles, our main battle tanks are also a weak point for our military. The vast majority of them are either over a decade old at this point, or just the scraps of the Japanese or American military handed out to some warlords we conquered. This is a state of affairs that can continue no longer.

The fact of the matter is, modern warfare is synonymous with armored warfare, and if we find ourselves unable to domestically produce armored fighting vehicles when the time comes to bear our arms against Germany, we will lose. Investing a small portion of our budget towards developing sufficient armor technology now is securing our future later.

directives.title: Innovate on the Kalashnikov
directives.desc:
The Kalashnikov assault rifle has become the gold standard for fighting in Russia, with each relevant contender for dominance fielding hundreds of Kalashnikov models for their armies, either Zlatoust originals or local made copies.

Despite its effectiveness and popularity, it is not a machine without flaws. Our engineers are promoting a series of improvements to the assault rifle, planning to make it lighter and more reliable with aims to give our mobile troops the edge they need.

directives.name: All Things in Union
directives.title: All Things in Union
directives.desc:
The challenge may have seemed insurmountable at first, but at last we can say that our administrative troubles are over. The last wounds of the Workers' Revolt have finally healed, while our new lands continue to adapt well to the Federation's laws.

More importantly, however, it seems our political disagreements with Barnaul have also been mended, at least for the time being. At last, President Pokryshkin is finally free to shape Siberia however he sees fit. With all the moving parts of our nation working in harmonious unison once again, our Federation will be reforged into a nation of iron; worthy of claiming the mantle of the legitimate Russian government!

NOV_the_victorious_federation.title: The Victorious Federation
NOV_the_victorious_federation.desc:

First there is the matter of consolidating our gains, by integrating the new territories more closely and securing our boundaries. Then we must consider how to stabilize our rule and satisfying the people, in hopes of restoring the law, order, and stability that is so desperately needed. Many problems remain, but beyond them lies a bright future for the Federation.

NOV_our_geopolitical_future.name: Our Geopolitical Future
NOV_our_geopolitical_future.title: Our Geopolitical Future
NOV_our_geopolitical_future.desc:
With the Federation's position secure, and Russia quickly stabilizing under our rule, we can begin looking outwards towards the world. Given the relatively non-ideological nature of our government, we find ourselves with great diplomatic opportunities.

Japan and its Sphere seem happy to deal with us and our corporations, as does the United States, which has even indicated it would support us in a conflict between us and Germany. The Federation's future is still uncertain, but if we can secure allies to help defend us, and trade agreements to reinforce our economy, there will be nothing we can't do.

NOV_bread_and_games.title: Bread and Games
NOV_bread_and_games.desc:

So long as these are provided and made easily accessible, there will be little cause for unhappiness and unrest among the people, and therefore very little room for extremist organizations to grow and gain strength.

While some sacrifices must be made to achieve this, they are more than worth the current and future stability of our state.

NOV_appoint_new_governors.name: Appoint New Governors
NOV_appoint_new_governors.title: Appoint New Governors
NOV_appoint_new_governors.desc:

Now that we are in a more secure position, it is finally time to make good on our promise to remove them, and appoint new ones in their place to aid the integration into the Federation of new lands, as well as the restoration of stability and reduction of popular unrest.

NOV_establish_educational_standards.name: Establish Educational Standards
NOV_establish_educational_standards.title: Establish Educational Standards
NOV_establish_educational_standards.desc:
How can we hope to cultivate a world-class economy when our people continue to go about their lives without an education to speak of? To say that our education system is in shambles would allude to the existence of such a system to begin with. In reality, any semblance of a proper schooling body fell into the abyss along with the rest of the Soviet Union over two decades ago.

Let us finally lay out the groundwork for a proper education system. We shall develop new curricula and guidelines for the classrooms, to make sure that the students of the Federation are being taught in the ways of the modern world.

NOV_repurpose_the_siberian_plan.title: Repurpose the Siberian Plan
NOV_repurpose_the_siberian_plan.desc:
Up until now, the Federation's industrial might has been built on the back of Bukharin's Siberian Plan. While the Siberian Plan was by far Bukharin's greatest achievement, it cannot be denied that the industrial base it was responsible for has been lagging behind in the march of progress.

We should use the plan as a template with which to create a modern and improved plan in order to meet the needs of a modern industrial state. It will be up to the industrial theorists and brilliant minds of the Federation to build this new plan, but when it is complete our industrial might will be unassailable within Russia.

However, attempts to make use of this natural bounty are impeded by the great disarray and inefficiency present in our agricultural sector, a problem that we are increasingly forced to give our attention to prevent it from worsening.

Fortunately for us, there is a simple solution to this, which is establishing firm and vigilant supervision of the whole sector, allowing us to streamline and organize it.

NOV_the_siberian_air_fleet.title: The Siberian Air Fleet
NOV_the_siberian_air_fleet.desc:
The air forces of the Federation have always been one of its greatest advantages, soaring above to rain fiery death upon those of our enemies unlucky enough to be below them, and shooting down any foolish enough to try and oppose them in the air.

NOV_incorporate_new_territorial_armies.title: Incorporate New Territorial Armies
NOV_incorporate_new_territorial_armies.desc:
Many of the lands conquered by the Federation fielded impressive armies when they still had their independence, even if they weren't so impressive as to be able to prevent defeat and annexation by us.

It would be wise to incorporate the best of these forces into our own military, growing it significantly and allowing us to have them fight those we face next. Though we must be cautious, so that our armed forces do not become infested with extremists, we also cannot afford to be too picky in these chaotic times.

NOV_travel_to_the_east.title: Travel to the East
NOV_travel_to_the_east.desc:

NOV_missions_to_our_neighborhood.name: Missions to Our Neighbors
NOV_missions_to_our_neighborhood.title: Missions to Our Neighbors
NOV_missions_to_our_neighborhood.desc:
Though we might seek allies abroad, it would be unwise to neglect those states neighboring us, allowing our relationships with them to deteriorate. These include the Kazakhs, their future long since tied to that of Russia, the Chinese, once our rivals in the east and now a promising opportunity, and the Mongols, caught between us and the Sphere.

Until Russia is reunited, conflict with outside states is one of the last things we can afford. Additionally, much of our economy depends on trade with our neighbors, and we must avoid lost profit where we can.

NOV_enshrine_the_silovik_state.name: Enshrine the Silovik State
NOV_enshrine_the_silovik_state.title: Enshrine the Silovik State
NOV_enshrine_the_silovik_state.desc:
We must push forward with the idea of a state built on the principles of national stabilization and strength above all else, and managed by military officers who have proven their competence.

Effective and capable men are necessary to unite all of Russia under the Federation, and the past failure of states such as the Central Siberian Republic, which thought of stability and security as secondary concerns, has only proven further the necessity of this structure for the sake of peace.

NOV_the_vestiges_of_revolt.name: The Vestiges of Revolt
NOV_the_vestiges_of_revolt.title: The Vestiges of Revolt
NOV_the_vestiges_of_revolt.desc:
The scars of the Workers' Revolt still remain, and if nothing is done soon they will continue to fester unabated. We must remind the working class of Siberia that no matter what their grievances may be with our administration, rebellion will not be tolerated.

In addition to repairing the damage still left over from the fighting, we will restore order to the industrial sectors of the region and let any potential dissenters know that we are still in charge. Several methods have been proposed, and it will ultimately be up to our wise and noble President to decide which would be the best course of action.

NOV_grants_for_research_and_development.title: Grants for Research and Development
NOV_grants_for_research_and_development.desc:
We're never going to be able to stay ahead of our rivals when the entire Federation still uses technological methods that wouldn't look out of date thirty years ago. Unfortunately, having an advanced society is a bit more complicated than just waiting for skilled scientists and technicians to appear.

To speed the process along, we shall strategically designate certain sectors within the nation to receive specialized grants to aid research and development. Once we grease the wheels a little, the next generation of scientists will be within our reach.

NOV_promote_the_national_champions.title: Promote the National Champions
NOV_promote_the_national_champions.desc:
The corporations of Feniks, Sibir, and Titan are the engines that keep the Siberian Federation rolling. Without their considerable economic power at our side, it is likely that we wouldn't have been able to come as far as we have. They provide boundless employment opportunities, unmatched industrial expertise, and most importantly economic growth beyond our wildest dreams.

Our national champions deserve a central role in the economy. This has been the case all along, of course, but it is time to make this arrangement official. The Federation shall march forward with its loyal corporations as its greatest weapon!

NOV_expand_the_factory_city.name: Expand the Factory City
NOV_expand_the_factory_city.title: Expand the Factory City
NOV_expand_the_factory_city.desc:
Novosibirsk is widely known as a "factory city"; an industrial lynchpin that is sometimes regarded as more of a giant factory than a place where people make their homes. Indeed, this city is the most industrialized in all of Siberia, and we see no reason why we shouldn't embrace this fact.

With the help of our loyal "national champions", Novosibirsk shall be expanded far beyond its current, already extensive capabilities. This city shall be one that never rests; where the factories stretch beyond that which the eye can see, and work day and night to build a stronger, safer future for all of us.

NOV_subsidies_for_mechanization.title: Subsidies for Mechanization
NOV_subsidies_for_mechanization.desc:
The Siberian peasantry has so long been utilizing awfully outdated methods and techniques, with some of them dating from the times of the Tsars. This backwardness produces two worrying consequences for our Federation: A low agricultural output and large swaths of our workforce being tied up in inefficient activities.

We will mechanize our countryside. With subsidies and loans, our farms will be able to afford the most modern machinery, rapidly increasing production and breaking our reliance on large numbers of manual laborers.

NOV_inspect_japanese_jets.title: Inspect Japanese Jets
NOV_inspect_japanese_jets.desc:

For the good of the Federation.

NOV_siberian_war_doctrines.name: Siberian War Doctrines
NOV_siberian_war_doctrines.title: Siberian War Doctrines
NOV_siberian_war_doctrines.desc:
Fighting across nearly the entire breadth of Siberia taught us much in the ways of fighting Siberian warfare. We came up against many forces, unique in their doctrines and methods of warfare, and though we did eventually come out victorious, there were certainly instances in which forces even smaller than our own managed to inflict heavy losses on us, and even eke out a few small tactical victories.

We should seek to incorporate these practices and doctrines that our fallen foes utilized, so that we might further professionalize our fighting force. We can only become stronger for it.

NOV_lessons_of_the_unification_wars.name: Lessons of the Unification Wars
NOV_lessons_of_the_unification_wars.title: Lessons of the Unification Wars
NOV_lessons_of_the_unification_wars.desc:
War is a punishing teacher, and every mistake made is an advantage given to the enemy. Throughout the Siberian Unification Wars we learned a great deal about our armed forces' effectiveness, its strengths, its skills, and most importantly, its weaknesses.

These past few wars have exposed some glaring weaknesses in our army. They taught us what our soldiers were good at, and what they were very poor at. These were hard-won lessons, and must not be forgotten as we work to improve and modernize our military doctrine. Let's ensure that our military isn't forced to learn these lessons again.

Russia has, at this point, had a decently long history with Japan, and much of it isn't good. Despite that, Japan remains one of the globe's foremost superpowers, and its influence, much like Germany's or the United States', stretches far across the globe.

It would be foolish of us not open diplomatic ties with the Sphere and start working on improving our relations. Besides, history needn't dictate the future. It so happens that our governments and economic setups are rather alike, and cooperation between our two nations could bring about great prosperity. Let us see what we make happen.

It would be foolish of us not open diplomatic ties with the Sphere and start working on improving our relations. Besides, history needn't dictate the future. It so happens that our governments and economic setups are rather alike, and cooperation between our two nations could bring about great prosperity. Let us see what we make happen.

NOV_the_twin_eagles.name: The Twin Eagles
NOV_the_twin_eagles.title: The Twin Eagles
NOV_the_twin_eagles.desc:
Across the Pacific, America enticingly beckons to us. Among the three great superpowers currently manipulating politics globally, the United States has shown itself to be the most stable of the three. Like ourselves, they recognize the benefits that business can bring, and utilize such industrial strengths to become one of the most powerful nations on Earth even before the Second World War.

Though there are those who wouldn't consider us as democratic as, say, the old Central Siberian Republic once was, the United States has demonstrated a willingness in the past to support such governments regardless provided they are working against Germany or Japan. We should exploit this by reaching out, and seeing what deals can be made.

NOV_partnerships_in_china.title: Partnerships in China
NOV_partnerships_in_china.desc:
In spite of domination and exploitation by the Japanese, China has become a truly large market, with easy and largely secure investments, and it only continues to grow as time passes.

Though their ability to act on their own is limited, we will reach out to them within the boundaries they possess under the watchful eye of the Sphere, and forge economic and strategic partnerships to whatever extent we can to strengthen both parties and allow us greater access to and influence in the markets of East Asia.

NOV_a_kazakh_consulate.name: A Kazakh Consulate
NOV_a_kazakh_consulate.title: A Kazakh Consulate
NOV_a_kazakh_consulate.desc:
For centuries, the futures of Kazakhstan and Russia have been inextricably linked, and the present is no different. Much like us, the Kazakhs have suffered tremendously from war, banditry, and abject poverty.

However, they have overcome these difficulties just as we did, and are beginning to recover their past greatness. We should immediately dispatch an emissary to reach out to them, in order to establish formal relations and celebrate the beginning of the end of our shared tribulations.

NOV_connections_with_mongolia.name: Connections with Mongolia
NOV_connections_with_mongolia.title: Connections with Mongolia
NOV_connections_with_mongolia.desc:
Caught between two worlds, one that of a rising sun beginning to set, and the other a Russian bear coming out of hibernation to avenge its humiliation, the Mongols must align with one or the other to protect themselves in an increasingly restless Asia.

Obviously, it would be in our best interest to make every effort to convince them of the benefits of aligning with us. We will initiate talks to improve our relationship with them, securing our trade in the region and ensuring a stable buffer state against the Sphere for the time being.

NOV_reward_our_allies.name: Reward Our Allies
NOV_reward_our_allies.title: Reward Our Allies
NOV_reward_our_allies.desc:
Promises are promises, and we made quite a few of them to our corporate friends during our time of crisis. Now that we are in less immediate danger, they expect these promises to be kept, and our government has always at least met expectations.

We shall grant them new and more generous contracts with the Federation, to allow them to expand into and exploit the resources of the new territories under our control. This will make their past investments into our cause profitable and convince them that continued cooperation with us would be in their best interest.

NOV_trust_in_the_party_of_power.name: Trust in the Party of Power
NOV_trust_in_the_party_of_power.title: Trust in the Party of Power
NOV_trust_in_the_party_of_power.name_en: Trust in the Party of Power
NOV_trust_in_the_party_of_power.title_en: Trust in the Party of Power
NOV_trust_in_the_party_of_power.desc:
What is needed above all else by the people is prosperity for them and stability of the state, and we cannot rely on popular will to bring this about. Democracy has failed us in the past, and giving it another chance would be a serious, and possibly fatal, mistake.

Instead, our objective should be solidifying our control over the state apparatus and levers of power, in order to centralize the powers of the government and give the people what they should have, even if it is not what they want.

NOV_a_nod_to_democracy.name: A Nod to Democracy
NOV_a_nod_to_democracy.title: A Nod to Democracy
NOV_a_nod_to_democracy.desc:
Though it might seem unwise to rely once more on a system that failed us all miserably, there is an argument to be made for allowing the masses a greater measure of democracy, mainly that it would serve to placate those hesitant to accept our government.

This would take the form of minor concessions and reforms within the state, as well as opening more leadership positions to civilians and supporters of democratic power. Of course, we would not go so far as to allow the people to have real power over us, but by appearing to scale back our control over them, they might be more eager to serve our purposes.

NOV_the_sovereign_security_act.name: The Sovereign Security Act
NOV_the_sovereign_security_act.title: The Sovereign Security Act
NOV_the_sovereign_security_act.desc:
No preventative measures are too drastic when the safety of our people is on the line! Terrorists and would-be revolutionaries lurk behind every corner, and our current means of dealing with them simply is not sufficient any longer. A stronger, more iron-fisted approach is necessary.

The Sovereign Security Act will be our savior in these dark times. Our counter-insurgency forces will enjoy increased funding and supplies to perform their duties with enhanced efficiency, while certain political liberties abused by our hidden foes will be cracked down on. This is not likely to be a popular act with our people, but hopefully they will realize the necessity of such measures when our streets are safe again.

NOV_sensible_concessions.name: Sensible Concessions
NOV_sensible_concessions.title: Sensible Concessions
NOV_sensible_concessions.desc:
Some would suggest that an iron-clad hand is necessary to prevent unrest amongst the labor, but they fail to realize that such methods would only inflame working man's anger even more. The last thing we need right now is to pour gasoline on the embers of the last disaster, so perhaps a different approach is needed.

We shall reach out to prominent union leaders and labor activists to work out some sort of arrangement that would be best for both parties. If successful, we will kill two birds with one stone: our workers will have no reason to revolt against us, and our industry can finally achieve its past glories. All that remains now is to make the arrangements.

NOV_consolidate_the_energy_sector.name: Consolidate the Energy Sector
NOV_consolidate_the_energy_sector.title: Consolidate the Energy Sector
NOV_consolidate_the_energy_sector.desc:
Under the soil of Siberia lie vast reserves of oil and natural gas, fuel hydrocarbons, the lifeblood of the modern age. Until now, those riches lay mostly unexplored, but that must end very soon. We must organize and consolidate the energy extraction industry.

No longer to be left in the hands of small companies and adventurers, the nature of this business demands intense capital, and our government will grant that. With the guarantee of profit to our private partners and investors by way of an established monopoly and government inputs, the Siberian energy sector will be genuinely efficient.

NOV_a_mind_to_living_standards.name: A Mind to Living Standards
NOV_a_mind_to_living_standards.title: A Mind to Living Standards
NOV_a_mind_to_living_standards.desc:
Economies exist to support states, and states, in turn, exist to support the lives of the people that live under them. Our economy, our state, neither are exempt from these rules. As we continue our efforts to reunite Russia, and our economy expands with our borders, so too will our state have to make use of this expanded economy to improve the lives of its citizens.

If we do not, we run the risk of inspiring a level of popular unrest we can't afford to have at such a critical moment. As such, we will devote more of our industrial output to the creation of various products that make the lives of consumers easier and more convenient.

NOV_realize_kamovs_designs.title: Realize Kamov's Designs
NOV_realize_kamovs_designs.desc:
Engineer Nikolai Kamov has designed some of the most impressive aircraft ever seen, unfortunately, unrealized because of their complexity. Now that our control of Siberia is secure, it's time to put those bold plans to fruition and start producing those flying machines.

The factories of Novosibirsk will start assembling Kamov's model of a coaxial rotor utility helicopter, unlike anything our enemies have. This fast mobile transport will give our troops a cutting edge on the battlefield.

NOV_revise_the_training_programs.name: Revise the Training Programs
NOV_revise_the_training_programs.title: Revise the Training Programs
NOV_revise_the_training_programs.desc:
Having incorporated many army's doctrines and many armies themselves into our military, we have discovered many inadequacies in our training regimens and army induction process as a whole.

It would do us well to rework our training corps so that we might start putting out more professionalized soldiers as we move away from the mercenary type training we used before, utilizing the doctrines and procedures we have adopted from these other subjugated warlords. Hopefully, this will allow us to improve our army's long term effectiveness.

NOV_propose_the_mongolian_pipeline.title: Propose the Mongolian Pipeline
NOV_propose_the_mongolian_pipeline.desc:
One of Japan's greatest weaknesses has always been natural resources. The ravenous Japanese economy simply never had enough on the home isles to sustain itself. It's a big part of why Japan went on to conquer so much of Asia. Their war machine simply could not function without the coal of Manchuria and oil of Indonesia.

Even now, an inefficient Sphere still struggles to keep up with the material demands of Japan. Fortunately for us, resources have always been among Russia's greatest strengths. We produce almost everything, and in great amounts as well. We should see if Japan wouldn't be opposed to the construction of a pipeline through Mongolia to facilitate materials trade between our two nations.

NOV_discuss_arctic_partnerships.name: Discuss Arctic Partnerships
NOV_discuss_arctic_partnerships.title: Discuss Arctic Partnerships
NOV_discuss_arctic_partnerships.desc:
Though relatively underutilized from a trade perspective, the Arctic region offers unique benefits for those around it - including ourselves.

For Russia, not only is it a viable trade route through which we can ship goods to the Atlantic now that we've lost the former Leningrad, but it is also an avenue through which we can exert our own political power and potentially align some nations with our own.

We should reach out to other Arctic countries, and see what economic partnerships can be made between our industrialists and theirs.

NOV_a_controlled_political_spectrum.name: A Controlled Political Spectrum
NOV_a_controlled_political_spectrum.title: A Controlled Political Spectrum
NOV_a_controlled_political_spectrum.desc:
Although they have little actual chance of taking power again, it's always wisest not to underestimate the ambitions of the extreme movements of the left and right.

In order to weaken them, and therefore strengthen our government, we will play them against each other, distracting them with their petty ideological struggle while convincing the people of their dangerous and violent nature, thereby slowly reducing them to irrelevancy without us having to act openly against them. By doing so, we will take control of all politics in the Federation, and keep the demagogues in check.

NOV_maintaining_the_equilibrium.name: Maintaining the Equilibrium
NOV_maintaining_the_equilibrium.title: Maintaining the Equilibrium
NOV_maintaining_the_equilibrium.desc:
For the first time in many months, our cities are finally returning to their pre-revolt orderliness, but there is still work to be done. Old ghosts from the unification wars still haunt our new territories to this very day, and they will need to be excorcized if our Federation wishes to move forward into a bold new future.

A heightened police presence will dissuade our new subjects from any foolish action, but a strong show of force is only half the battle. Meetings will be held with the provincial governors and mayors across Siberia to discuss the best way to finish the integration of these troubled lands. With luck, we won't have to give too many concessions in the name of stability.

NOV_the_riches_of_siberia2.title: The Riches of Siberia
NOV_the_riches_of_siberia2.desc:
As we continue to expand our industrial base it will be imperative to keep up a constant flow of resources to feed the engines of progress. Thankfully, the lands of Siberia are rich with the natural resources that will be essential to driving our ever growing economic needs.

With the aid of our good friends and allies in the National Champions it is only a matter of time before the vast wealth of Siberia will be available to us in quantities unheard of before.

The riches of Siberia must be exploited for the good of the Federation.

NOV_a_central_design_bureau.name: A Central Design Bureau
NOV_a_central_design_bureau.title: A Central Design Bureau
NOV_a_central_design_bureau.desc:
Research of new and improved technologies and designs to implement them for practical use are critical to the advancement of our state, but both have a certain risk to them. Left uncontrolled and undirected, research and design can easily become useless, or even counterproductive.

To protect against this and ensure efficient and coordinated scientific work, we will establish a Central Design Bureau, responsible for oversight of all practical research, the design of new technologies, and the organization of all scientific efforts.

NOV_a_bipolar_partnership.name: A Bipolar Partnership
NOV_a_bipolar_partnership.title: A Bipolar Partnership
NOV_a_bipolar_partnership.desc:
At last, we have taken the necessary steps towards decisively aligning ourselves with a powerful Pacific government and deepening the association between us, finally creating a partnership with them certain to stand the test of time.

While this decision came with no shortage of controversy from those who had favored a deal with the other power, it is done and there is nothing they can do about it now. There is little reason for them to be bitter, either; we have reaped great rewards from our improved trade with our chosen partners, and the benefits have been seen by everyone that matters.

NOV_consider_barnauls_position.name: Consider Barnaul's Position
NOV_consider_barnauls_position.title: Consider Barnaul's Position
NOV_consider_barnauls_position.desc:
Novosibirsk may be the administrative center of the Federation, but the adjacent city of Barnaul is also an important lynchpin in our nation. Its mayor, Vasily Shukshin, has quickly grown to be the second most powerful politician within the halls of power, and his particular views on how the state should be run have become more prominent as well.

Unfortunately, Shukshin's rise has caused some rather predictable tension with his main rival: President Pokryshkin. In order to put a stop to this bickering before it gets out of control, perhaps it would be prudent to reach out to Shukshin and see if he's willing to compromise in some way.

NOV_active_measures.name: Active Measures
NOV_active_measures.title: Active Measures
NOV_active_measures.desc:
There are many ways one can influence the course of history to their liking. Some of these methods may appear small, but make big changes in the grand scheme of things. After all, if a ship changes its course only slightly, the destination shall be entirely different. In this instance, our destination is a strong and stable Russia.

Our security forces are no stranger to manipulating the chain of events to suit our purposes. A few dishonest media campaigns here, a counterfeit document or two there... all our agents must do is pull a few hidden strings, and the minds of our people will be forever focused in a more suitable direction. After all, an ignorant citizen is a content citizen...

NOV_special_administrative_zones.name: Special Administrative Zones
NOV_special_administrative_zones.title: Special Administrative Zones
NOV_special_administrative_zones.desc:
Our foes during the unification wars were a diverse bunch, if nothing else. From the mad monarchists of Kemerovo to the armchair philosophers and artists of Tomsk; they all had vastly different approaches to governing their lands, and bafflingly enough? Most of them worked.

Why change what is already working? As long as these regions remain loyal to us, there is no need to crack down on them. "Special Administrative Zones" have been established in these formerly hostile territories to continue the administrative methods of their previous owners, while still bringing them in line with our own ideals of governance. Any regions whose administration cannot be adapted, however, can always be granted to our friends in the industrial sector...

NOV_infantry_support_vehicle_designs.name: Infantry Support Vehicle Designs
NOV_infantry_support_vehicle_designs.title: Infantry Support Vehicle Designs
NOV_infantry_support_vehicle_designs.desc:
Modern warfare requires vehicles that are both capable and reliable. Operating across the vast distances and in the harsh climate of Siberia, we have become well accustomed in what makes an effective vehicle.

Despite that, we remain dependent on foreign or pre-war vehicles for almost all of our needs. Not only are these foreign goods of dubious quality when they arrive here, they are often not suited for the demands we place on them. We will, therefore, design new, domestic vehicles specifically for our needs in this demanding environment, and in so doing ensure our army's effectiveness and viability.

NOV_a_siberian_mbt.name: A Siberian MBT
NOV_a_siberian_mbt.title: A Siberian MBT
NOV_a_siberian_mbt.desc:
In a similar vein to our motorized vehicles, our main battle tanks are also a weak point for our military. The vast majority of them are either over a decade old at this point, or just the scraps of the Japanese or American military handed out to some warlords we conquered. This is a state of affairs that can continue no longer.

The fact of the matter is, modern warfare is synonymous with armored warfare, and if we find ourselves unable to domestically produce armored fighting vehicles when the time comes to bear our arms against Germany, we will lose. Investing a small portion of our budget towards developing sufficient armor technology now is securing our future later.

NOV_innovate_on_the_kalashnikov.title: Innovate on the Kalashnikov
NOV_innovate_on_the_kalashnikov.desc:
The Kalashnikov assault rifle has become the gold standard for fighting in Russia, with each relevant contender for dominance fielding hundreds of Kalashnikov models for their armies, either Zlatoust originals or local made copies.

Despite its effectiveness and popularity, it is not a machine without flaws. Our engineers are promoting a series of improvements to the assault rifle, planning to make it lighter and more reliable with aims to give our mobile troops the edge they need.

NOV_all_things_in_union.name: All Things in Union
NOV_all_things_in_union.title: All Things in Union
NOV_all_things_in_union.desc:
The challenge may have seemed insurmountable at first, but at last we can say that our administrative troubles are over. The last wounds of the Workers' Revolt have finally healed, while our new lands continue to adapt well to the Federation's laws.

More importantly, however, it seems our political disagreements with Barnaul have also been mended, at least for the time being. At last, President Pokryshkin is finally free to shape Siberia however he sees fit. With all the moving parts of our nation working in harmonious unison once again, our Federation will be reforged into a nation of iron; worthy of claiming the mantle of the legitimate Russian government!
